literal: Millet-measure-becoming fault even-if-comes palm-measure-as they-will-consider blame those-who-fear.
translation: Those who shrink from disgrace will consider a fault as big as a palm tree, even if it is only the size of a millet seed.
modern: பழிக்கு அஞ்சுகின்றவர்கள், தினை அளவு சிறிய குற்றம் வந்தாலும், அதனைப் பனை அளவு பெரியதாகக் கருதுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the tiny millet seed with the massive palmyra tree to illustrate how the virtuous view their own mistakes. Those who deeply fear disgrace do not dismiss small errors. Instead, they magnify even the slightest fault to ensure they maintain their moral integrity.
